novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed strict extension is benchmarked only against SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 and remains one fixed symmetric contrast, not a generic contrast class or a two-comparator frontier, so flagship framing is capped at field.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Theorems 2.1–2.3, lines 49–60 and 93–134; Theorem 3.1, lines 128–163; Appendix C, lines 432–437.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper treats two binary potential outcomes, proves an unrestricted-design reduction to a scalar binomial experiment, and proves rho_n*=n^-1-(-4^(1/3)a'_1)n^(-4/3)+o(n^(-4/3)), attained by balanced Bernoulli assignment and nonlinear shrinkage.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract, lines 39–42; Section 1, lines 54–71; Theorem 1, lines 142–152; discussion, lines 161–176.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Hull studies a two-treatment bounded-outcome finite-population ATE game; independent assignment remains minimax under arbitrary measurable estimators, with a nonlinear endpoint-rule convex program. The paper identifies Sudijono et al. as the sharp second-order companion.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and Theorem 2.1 description in the published PDF.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Bai studies finite-sample minimax randomization under permutation-invariant distribution classes; complete randomization is minimax for a given assignment vector and, with additional conditions, linear estimation uses difference-in-means or blockwise differences with Neyman allocation.

The paper develops design-based finite-sample and asymptotic properties of OLS/RLS covariate adjustment in multi-arm and factorial experiments; it is regular regression-adjustment theory, not a sharp unrestricted minimax expansion.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Move the lossless exact orbit-game equality into an explicitly imported result from exp_multiarm_secondorder_minimax_frontier, and make the half-wedge constant, uniform bridge, and allocation frontier the only new kernel claims.

Promote the sharp theorem from the single symmetric contrast to a stated open class of three-arm contrasts, proving the tangent-cone chart and the two-arm embedded-submodel reduction uniformly; this clears the single-comparator-chain ceiling.

Add a certified finite-n table for the eight-type game at several n, including the n=3 labelled gap and allocation perturbations of order n^(-1/6), with rigorous rational enclosures for the proposed C3 correction.

recommended_next_step: Revise around the accepted repository parent: import its finite orbit reduction, retain the new sharp half-wedge problem, and either explicitly frame the result as field-tier or generalize it beyond one contrast.
